assertions: Sir William Waller, not Sir Ralph Hopton, will overcome in the engagement near Alresford (the Battle of Cheriton) on 29 March 1644
Hopton's army will be defeated and forced to retreat and give ground, unable to hold the field against Waller

Waller's assistance and substance are strong and honourable: the Sun, lord of his substance/assistants, in the 10th in the very degree of his exaltation (19 degrees Aries), so his supporters will sustain him effectively in the fight
Hopton will receive no ready supplies or effective assistance, signified by only Mars and the South Node in the 9th house
Hopton himself is in a weak, isolated and dishonoured condition: his significator Saturn is in his fall, peregrine, sub radiis, in no aspect to any planet, and aspecting the cusp of the 7th by square
Momentum grows for Waller's side during the engagement: the Moon, his co-significator, is in her exaltation with Jupiter, swift and increasing in light, and 11 degrees distant from Venus
method: Classical horary astrology (Lilly, whole-sign/ classical dignities): Ascendant and Moon, Jupiter and Venus for Waller's side against Saturn lord of the 7th for Hopton
reasoning: Waller's significators are essentially and accidentally strong: Moon exalted and with Jupiter (great benefic), Sun lord of his substance/assistants exalted exactly at 19 Aries in the angular 10th of honour, and Moon swift and increasing in light. Hopton's significator Saturn is in fall, peregrine, sub radiis, unaspected and squaring his own 7th cusp, with no supplies ready (only Mars and South Node in the 9th). Strength, assistance and momentum are all on Waller's side, debility and isolation on Hopton's, so Waller overcomes.
summary: Waller will overcome Hopton at Cheriton.
